message.reasoning:
I need to write JUnit 4 tests for the DataUtil class, placing them in the org.jsoup.helper package so I can access the package-private methods. I'm mapping out which methods need coverage, including the public load overloads and package-private helpers like crossStreams and parseInputStream.

My coverage plan includes readToByteBuffer, readFileToByteBuffer, emptyByteBuffer, charset detection, mime boundary generation, and BOM detection, plus detailed branch coverage for parseInputStream's charset resolution logic -- null input handling, BOM-based charset detection, meta tag parsing for charset declarations, XML encoding declarations, and the re-decoding logic when the detected charset differs from the default.

I also need to trace through the charsetName validation path (empty string throwing exceptions), the BufferedReader fallback path when doc is null, and the getCharsetFromContentType/validateCharset branches covering null, empty, valid, and unsupported charset cases, plus mimeBoundary length checks and the negative maxSize validation in readToByteBuffer.

Now I'm mapping out remaining cases: unlimited vs limited reads based on maxSize, normal file-to-buffer conversion, empty buffer capacity checks, stream copying, and BOM detection via parseInputStream. With that coverage planned, I'm ready to start writing the actual test class in the same package as DataUtil so I can access its package-private methods, setting up temp files and ByteArrayInputStreams with various charset and meta-tag scenarios to exercise each branch.

For test 2, I'll feed a stream explicitly UTF-8 encoded with a given charset and verify the resulting document's output charset matches. Then for test 3, I'm checking that passing an empty charset name throws an IllegalArgumentException.

Test 4 will construct HTML with a meta http-equiv tag specifying ISO-8859-1 encoding in a byte stream, so I can confirm the parser correctly detects and applies the charset from the meta tag rather than the one passed explicitly.

Test 5 checks the same detection logic but using an HTML5 meta charset attribute instead, and Test 6 verifies charset detection from an XML declaration header, though I need to confirm whether the default HTML parser or the XML parser is used for that case.

Test 7 covers the scenario where no charset is specified anywhere in the document, so the default UTF-8 should be used, with the stream fully read since the content is shorter than the buffer size.

Test 8 checks that parsing an input stream handles a UTF-8 BOM correctly.

Since doc is still null, the code reads the stream with UTF-8 charset and skips the BOM byte since UTF-8's offset flag is true, then parses normally and sets output charset to UTF-8 -- I should verify the BOM bytes don't leak into the parsed text. Next I'm checking a UTF-16 BOM test case where the offset flag is false, meaning no skip occurs, since the BOM bytes themselves are part of the encoding there.

Since offset is false for UTF-16, I'm reasoning that Java's InputStreamReader auto-detects and strips the BOM when given the generic "UTF-16" charset name, so the test should still parse correctly. I'm considering whether to include a UTF-32 BOM test too, weighing JDK charset support concerns against keeping the test suite focused, and deciding to include the important cases without overdoing it. Now I'm moving on to examine the getCharsetFromContentType method and its null-input branch.

For getCharsetFromContentType, I'm planning cases: no content type returns null, a type without charset returns null, "charset=UTF-8" extracts correctly, an invalid charset name falls back to null, and quoted charset values parse properly, which also indirectly covers validateCharset. For mimeBoundary(), I'm checking the generated boundary matches the expected length and only uses allowed characters. For readToByteBuffer, I'm testing that a negative maxSize throws an exception, zero reads everything, and a positive maxSize limits the read -- though without seeing ConstrainableInputStream's exact behavior, I'll keep the assertions loose and just confirm the returned buffer's limit stays within a reasonable bound of maxSize.

I'm also planning tests for readFileToByteBuffer to verify byte-for-byte matching against a known file, emptyByteBuffer to confirm zero capacity and remaining, and crossStreams to check that content copied from an InputStream to an OutputStream matches exactly. Then I'll add load(File) and load(InputStream) tests using a temp HTML file to verify the parsed document's title and structure come out correctly.

I also want to verify that loading a nonexistent file throws FileNotFoundException, and confirm Validate.notEmpty catches blank charset names during stream parsing. Now I'm drafting the actual test class with the necessary imports for jsoup parsing, JUnit assertions, temp folder rules, and NIO buffer/charset utilities.

For the meta-tag detection tests, I'm constructing HTML with a Content-Type meta tag specifying ISO-8859-1 encoding, then encoding the string to raw bytes in that charset so the parser has to detect it from the byte stream itself.

Then I'm tracing through parseInputStream: it initially decodes as UTF-8 (which is safe since the tags are ASCII and malformed bytes just get replaced), detects the declared charset from the meta tag, confirms it differs from the default, and triggers a re-decode using the correct charset.

Now I'm setting up test cases—one verifying the body text decodes correctly as "café" and the output charset matches ISO-8859-1, another using a meta charset attribute variant, and a third for testing XML declarations.

For the XML test, I'm constructing an ISO-8859-1 encoded document with an explicit XML declaration specifying that encoding, then parsing it with jsoup's XML parser to verify the charset gets correctly detected from the XmlDeclaration node rather than a meta tag.

I also want to verify the decoded text matches "café" and that the output settings reflect the right charset, plus test the fallback case where no charset is specified anywhere—checking whether jsoup defaults to UTF-8 in that scenario.

Now I'm writing a BOM detection test: I construct a byte stream with a UTF-8 BOM prefix followed by simple HTML content, parse it through DataUtil, and verify the resulting document reports UTF-8 as its charset while correctly stripping the BOM from the body text.

That skip(1) removes the single decoded BOM character, matching the expected "hello" output. Now checking the UTF-16 BOM case with offset=false, where the BOM bytes are prepended separately before the UTF-16BE encoded content, and considering how InputStreamReader handles the generic "UTF-16" charset name.

Java's StreamDecoder actually auto-detects endianness from the BOM for generic "UTF-16", consuming it automatically even without an explicit skip, so it should still yield clean text without the BOM character showing up.

I'll verify the charset name and body text come out correct. For UTF-32, I'm hesitant since support varies across JVMs -- I'll either include it cautiously with a note about potential compatibility issues, or skip it entirely to avoid flaky test failures.

I'm testing this indirectly through parseInputStream for UTF-8 and UTF-16, since directly accessing the private BOM detection method via reflection is impractical. Now I need to pin down how Validate.notEmpty behaves -- I recall jsoup's implementation throws an IllegalArgumentException when the string is null or empty.

For the crossStreams test, I'm feeding a simple byte stream through the method and asserting the output bytes match the input exactly. For readToByteBuffer, I'm covering negative size (should throw), zero (reads everything), and a positive limit smaller than the data to check truncation behavior with ConstrainableInputStream.

I'm also planning tests for readFileToByteBuffer using a temp file, emptyByteBuffer checking zero capacity, getCharsetFromContentType, and mimeBoundary verifying length 32 with allowed characters only, plus a load(File,...) test writing out an html file to parse.

Then I want to cover more load() variants: null charset, explicit charset, FileNotFoundException on missing files, and an InputStream load with an explicit Parser. Since these target package-private methods in org.jsoup.helper, I need to place the test class in that same package and import the Document class to verify parsing results.

I also need to add JUnit's TemporaryFolder rule and exception-expecting test annotations, plus a helper for concatenating byte arrays for BOM tests, before writing out the full test suite with descriptive method names.

I'll confirm defaultCharset and boundaryLength are package-private fields accessible directly from the test class, and work out the exact byte count needed in the no-charset scenario so fullyRead comes out true and the document is preserved rather than nulled.

For the default output charset when no charset is found, I'm fairly confident jsoup's Document defaults to UTF-8 in its OutputSettings, though this isn't explicitly shown in the source I've seen -- I'll go with this well-known default rather than treating it as pure speculation.

To be cautious, though, I should avoid asserting the exact charset name for that scenario and instead just verify doc is parsed correctly (title/body text present), noting why I'm skipping the charset check.

For the BOM UTF-8 case, though, the charset assertion is safe since doc stays null until the explicit branch runs setting outputSettings charset to "UTF-8" directly from the source.

Similarly, in the meta-charset-found case (ISO-8859-1), doc is explicitly nulled and reparsed, then outputSettings().charset() is explicitly set to ISO-8859-1, so that assertion is safe too. But in the no-charset-found scenario where doc stays from the initial parse call, DataUtil never explicitly sets the charset, so I shouldn't assume what the default Document constructor does there -- I'll skip that charset assertion and just verify the body text and that doc isn't null.

For the "" charsetName case, I expect Validate.notEmpty to trigger IllegalArgumentException, which is the common pattern in jsoup's Validate helper, though I should flag that this isn't directly confirmed since the Validate class source wasn't provided.

I'll note the same caveat for the readToByteBuffer negative maxSize test, which relies on Validate.isTrue similarly throwing IllegalArgumentException. I'll also add a boundary test for maxSize=0 to confirm unlimited reading behavior before writing out the complete file.
